canonical_answers: Energy conservation gives maximum compression x=0.200 m.

payload.text: A 0.500 kg cart moving at 4.00 m/s compresses an ideal spring of constant 200 N/m on a level frictionless track.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies the cart's incoming speed as the independent variable, the maximum spring compression distance as the dependent variable, and holds the cart's mass and the spring constant fixed as the control.
required_evidence: cart's incoming speed as the independent variable
maximum compression distance as the dependent variable
cart mass and spring constant held constant as the control
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why converting all of the cart's kinetic energy into ideal-spring potential energy, assuming no friction acts on the track, justifies the 0.200 m compression result.

criteria.description: Correctly cites conservation of mechanical energy as the governing principle and states that the track is assumed frictionless and the spring ideal.
required_evidence: kinetic energy converts entirely to spring potential energy
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.

accessibility.accommodation_notes: Text and symbolic notation are fully described.

review_notes.expected_reasoning: Energy conservation gives maximum compression x=0.200 m.
